Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3-day history of worsening, predominantly right-sided, dull→sharp headache (pain score 8/10)  
  • Photophobia and “shooting lights”; no nausea/vomiting, no focal neurologic deficits, no fever, rash, or recent head injury  
  • Possible migraine given personal symptoms and positive family history
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Mother – recurrent migraines (seasonal trigger)  
  • Sister – infrequent migraines
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Ibuprofen (patient self-taken, 3 tablets per day; exact dose/strength not documented)  
  • No regular prescribed medications
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded (clinician asked about oral contraceptive pill; patient did not answer).
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Social smoker  
  • Social alcohol use  
  • No other substances mentioned
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  • Reports some work-related stress; no anxiety or depressive symptoms disclosed
- Vision problems or recent changes:
  • Photophobia with current headache  
  • “Weird shooting lights” at onset  
  • Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye examination
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with three housemates  
  • Works in IT; current headache affecting screen-based work  
  • No caring responsibilities mentioned

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums): Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen): Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria): Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not applicable (age 26) / Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Provided education that presentation is suggestive of migraine.
- Advised correct dosing of Ibuprofen (up to 2 tablets three times daily) OR prescription offered for stronger NSAID (Naproxen) ± Paracetamol/Codeine.
- Recommended keeping a headache diary to identify triggers.
- Suggested arranging an eye test if visual strain persists.
- Safety-net advice: return or call sooner for worsening headache, visual changes, limb weakness, or if unwell.
- Follow-up appointment in 1–2 weeks to reassess headache frequency and consider prophylactic therapy if needed.

Consider (not performed in consult):
- CTG registration, preventive health checks, and allied health or mental health referrals as indicated at future review.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: BP, pulse, weight/BMI, waist circumference, dental/ear/eye screening, urinalysis, immunisation review, detailed alcohol/smoking quantification, mental health screening (K10/PHQ-9), sexual history and contraception, cervical screening status, baseline pathology.  
● No internal contradictions noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational fillers but clinical content understandable.
